definitions.explanation: A room or building where prisoners are kept. Often evokes a traditional or historical image of confinement, such as cells with bars.

examples.japanese: {牢屋|ろうや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れられた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
⟦{犯人|はんにん}→犯人：03572_hannin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{暗|くら}い→暗い：00647_kurai⟧{牢屋|ろうや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{過|す}ごした→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧。
examples.english: The criminal spent time in a dark prison cell.

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{牢屋|ろうや}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{刑務所|けいむしょ}→刑務所：19074_keimusho⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧まったく⟦{違|ちが}っていた→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Jails in the Edo period were completely different from today's prisons.

notes:
USAGE:
{牢屋|ろうや} has a somewhat old-fashioned or dramatic tone. In modern everyday language, ⟦{刑務所|けいむしょ}→刑務所：19074_keimusho⟧ (prison) is the standard term for penal institutions. {牢屋|ろうや} is commonly used in historical contexts, fiction, and colloquial expressions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牢屋|ろうや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ (to put in jail)
- {牢屋|ろうや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (to go to jail)
- {牢屋|ろうや}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (to get out of jail)
